transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

It is very unlikely you need a new one yet. With Shark uprights, gradual suction loss like yours is almost always caused by either a blockage or dirty/wet filters rather than motor failure. These machines rely on clean, bone-dry filters to maintain airflow. If they were washed recently but not left to dry for at least 24 hours, residual moisture can block air passage just like a solid plug. Alternatively, if they haven't been washed in a while, fine dust may have clogged the mesh. Could you check whether the pre-motor and HEPA filters are clean and completely dry? If they look dirty or feel damp, wash them in cold water only (no detergent) and let them air-dry fully for 24 hours before putting them back. If they are already clean and dry, we will then need to check for a physical blockage in the hose or floorhead.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

I've never washed them, didn't know they were there. Found them under the bin. The foam one is solid grey and the felt one is caked with fine dust. No burning smell or anything like that. Should I wash them?

Yes, please wash both the foam and felt filters in cold water only (no detergent). After washing, squeeze out excess water gently and leave them to air-dry completely for at least 24 hours before putting them back. It is critical that they are bone-dry; if you put damp filters back in, suction will remain weak or the motor could be damaged.
